chunks: When Adam circumambulated the House (Kaaba) and arrived at Al-Multazam, Jibrail (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O Adam, acknowledge your sins to your Lord in this place.'
He (the narrator) said: So Adam (peace be upon him) stopped and said: 'O my Lord, for every doer of deeds there is a recompense, and I have done deeds, so what is my recompense?'
So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Adam, I have forgiven your sin.'

He said: 'O my Lord, and for my children, or for my offspring?' So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Adam, whoever from your offspring comes to this place, acknowledges his sins, and repents just as you repented, then seeks forgiveness, I will forgive him.'

key_terms.أقرّ: To acknowledge, confess, make a formal admission of one's sins
key_terms.الاستغفار: Seeking forgiveness — explicitly asking God for pardon after repentance
key_terms.التوبة: Repentance — turning back to God with sincere contrition
key_terms.الذنب: Sin, transgression; specifically Adam's original transgression
key_terms.الملتزم: Al-Multazam — the section of the Kaaba between the Black Stone (Hajar al-Aswad) and the door; a place of supplication

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Al-Multazam in Islam and why did Adam (AS) pray there?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the story of Adam (AS) performing tawaf around the Kaaba in its primordial context. After being instructed by the angel Jibrail (AS) to confess his sins at Al-Multazam — the section of the Kaaba wall between the Black Stone and the door — Adam (AS) makes a profound supplication: he acknowledges that deeds deserve recompense and asks God what his recompense would be. God's response is forgiveness. Adam (AS) then intercedes for all his descendants, securing a divine promise that any of them who comes to Al-Multazam, confesses their sins with sincere repentance, and seeks forgiveness will also be forgiven. This hadith establishes the sacred status of Al-Multazam as a place of divine mercy and the spiritual precedent for confession and repentance in Islamic ritual.
